description: This module fetches data from the instance metadata endpoint in EC2 as per https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSEC2/latest/UserGuide/ec2-instance-metadata.html.

parameters.name: metadata_token_ttl_seconds
parameters.description: Specify a value for the X-aws-ec2-metadata-token-ttl-seconds header. Value must be between 1 and 21600. Default: 60

examples:
# Gather EC2 metadata facts
- amazon.aws.ec2_metadata_facts:

# Set a bigger value for X-aws-ec2-metadata-token-ttl-seconds header
- amazon.aws.ec2_metadata_facts:
    metadata_token_ttl_seconds: 240

- debug:
    msg: "This instance is a t1.micro"
  when: ansible_ec2_instance_type == "t1.micro"

return_values.name: ansible_ec2_ami_id
return_values.description: The AMI ID used to launch the instance. Returned: success Sample: "ami-XXXXXXXX"

return_values.name: ansible_ec2_ami_launch_index
return_values.description: If you started more than one instance at the same time, this value indicates the order in which the instance was launched. The value of the first instance launched is 0. Returned: success Sample: "0"

return_values.name: ansible_ec2_ami_manifest_path
return_values.description: The path to the AMI manifest file in Amazon S3. If you used an Amazon EBS-backed AMI to launch the instance, the returned result is unknown. Returned: success Sample: "(unknown)"

return_values.name: ansible_ec2_ancestor_ami_ids
return_values.description: The AMI IDs of any instances that were rebundled to create this AMI. This value will only exist if the AMI manifest file contained an ancestor-amis key. Returned: success Sample: "(unknown)"

return_values.name: ansible_ec2_block_device_mapping_ami
return_values.description: The virtual device that contains the root/boot file system. Returned: success Sample: "/dev/sda1"

return_values.name: ansible_ec2_block_device_mapping_ebsN
return_values.description: The virtual devices associated with Amazon EBS volumes, if any are present. Amazon EBS volumes are only available in metadata if they were present at launch time or when the instance was last started. The N indicates the index of the Amazon EBS volume (such as ebs1 or ebs2). Returned: success Sample: "/dev/xvdb"

return_values.name: ansible_ec2_block_device_mapping_ephemeralN
return_values.description: The virtual devices associated with ephemeral devices, if any are present. The N indicates the index of the ephemeral volume. Returned: success Sample: "/dev/xvdc"

return_values.name: ansible_ec2_block_device_mapping_root
return_values.description: The virtual devices or partitions associated with the root devices, or partitions on the virtual device, where the root (/ or C) file system is associated with the given instance. Returned: success Sample: "/dev/sda1"

return_values.name: ansible_ec2_block_device_mapping_swap
return_values.description: The virtual devices associated with swap. Not always present. Returned: success Sample: "/dev/sda2"

return_values.name: ansible_ec2_fws_instance_monitoring
return_values.description: Value showing whether the customer has enabled detailed one-minute monitoring in CloudWatch. Returned: success Sample: "enabled"

return_values.name: ansible_ec2_hostname
return_values.description: The private IPv4 DNS hostname of the instance. In cases where multiple network interfaces are present, this refers to the eth0 device (the device for which the device number is 0). Returned: success Sample: "ip-10-0-0-1.ec2.internal"

return_values.name: ansible_ec2_iam_info
return_values.description: If there is an IAM role associated with the instance, contains information about the last time the instance profile was updated, including the instance’s LastUpdated date, InstanceProfileArn, and InstanceProfileId. Otherwise, not present. Returned: success Sample: ""

return_values.name: InstanceProfileArn
return_values.description: The ARN of the InstanceProfile associated with the Instance. Returned: success

return_values.name: InstanceProfileId
return_values.description: The Id of the InstanceProfile associated with the Instance. Returned: success

return_values.name: LastUpdated
return_values.description: The last time which InstanceProfile is associated with the Instance changed. Returned: success

return_values.name: ansible_ec2_iam_info_instanceprofilearn

return_values.name: ansible_ec2_iam_info_instanceprofileid

return_values.name: ansible_ec2_iam_info_lastupdated

return_values.name: ansible_ec2_iam_instance_profile_role

return_values.name: ansible_ec2_iam_security_credentials_role_name
return_values.description: If there is an IAM role associated with the instance, role-name is the name of the role, and role-name contains the temporary security credentials associated with the role. Otherwise, not present. Returned: success Sample: ""

return_values.name: ansible_ec2_iam_security_credentials_role_name_type
return_values.description: IAM role type. Returned: success Sample: "AWS-HMAC"

return_values.name: ansible_ec2_instance_action

return_values.name: ansible_ec2_instance_tags
return_values.description: The dict of tags for the instance. Returns empty dict if access to tags (InstanceMetadataTags) in instance metadata is not enabled. Returned: success Sample: {"tagKey1": "tag value 1", "tag_key2": "tag value 2"}

return_values.name: ansible_ec2_instance_tags_keys
return_values.description: The list of tags keys of the instance. Returns empty list if access to tags (InstanceMetadataTags) in instance metadata is not enabled. Returned: success Sample: ["tagKey1", "tag_key2"]

return_values.name: ansible_ec2_mac
return_values.description: The instance’s media access control (MAC) address. In cases where multiple network interfaces are present, this refers to the eth0 device (the device for which the device number is 0). Returned: success Sample: "00:11:22:33:44:55"

return_values.name: ansible_ec2_metrics_vhostmd

return_values.name: ansible_ec2_network_interfaces_macs_mac_address_device_number
return_values.description: The unique device number associated with that interface. The device number corresponds to the device name; for example, a device-number of 2 is for the eth2 device. This category corresponds to the DeviceIndex and device-index fields that are used by the Amazon EC2 API and the EC2 commands for the AWS CLI. Returned: success Sample: "0"

return_values.name: ansible_ec2_network_interfaces_macs_mac_address_interface_id

return_values.description: The IPv6 addresses associated with the interface. Returned only for instances launched into a VPC. Returned: success Sample: ""

return_values.name: ansible_ec2_network_interfaces_macs_mac_address_local_hostname

return_values.name: ansible_ec2_network_interfaces_macs_mac_address_local_ipv4s

return_values.name: ansible_ec2_network_interfaces_macs_mac_address_mac
return_values.description: The instance’s MAC address. Returned: success Sample: "00:11:22:33:44:55"

return_values.name: ansible_ec2_network_interfaces_macs_mac_address_owner_id
return_values.description: The ID of the owner of the network interface. In multiple-interface environments, an interface can be attached by a third party, such as Elastic Load Balancing. Traffic on an interface is always billed to the interface owner. Returned: success Sample: "123456789012"

return_values.name: ansible_ec2_network_interfaces_macs_mac_address_public_hostname
return_values.description: The interface’s public DNS (IPv4). If the instance is in a VPC, this category is only returned if the enableDnsHostnames attribute is set to true. Returned: success Sample: "ec2-1-2-3-4.compute-1.amazonaws.com"

return_values.name: ansible_ec2_network_interfaces_macs_mac_address_public_ipv4s
return_values.description: The Elastic IP addresses associated with the interface. There may be multiple IPv4 addresses on an instance. Returned: success Sample: "1.2.3.4"

return_values.name: ansible_ec2_network_interfaces_macs_mac_address_security_group_ids
return_values.description: The IDs of the security groups to which the network interface belongs. Returned only for instances launched into a VPC. Returned: success Sample: "sg-01234567,sg-01234568"

return_values.name: ansible_ec2_network_interfaces_macs_mac_address_security_groups
return_values.description: Security groups to which the network interface belongs. Returned only for instances launched into a VPC. Returned: success Sample: "secgroup1,secgroup2"

return_values.name: ansible_ec2_network_interfaces_macs_mac_address_subnet_id
return_values.description: The ID of the subnet in which the interface resides. Returned only for instances launched into a VPC. Returned: success Sample: "subnet-01234567"

return_values.name: ansible_ec2_network_interfaces_macs_mac_address_subnet_ipv6_cidr_blocks

return_values.name: ansible_ec2_network_interfaces_macs_mac_address_vpc_id

return_values.name: ansible_ec2_network_interfaces_macs_mac_address_vpc_ipv4_cidr_block
return_values.description: The IPv4 CIDR block of the VPC in which the interface resides. Returned only for instances launched into a VPC. Returned: success Sample: "10.0.0.0/16"

return_values.name: ansible_ec2_network_interfaces_macs_mac_address_vpc_ipv4_cidr_blocks
return_values.description: The IPv4 CIDR block of the VPC in which the interface resides. Returned only for instances launched into a VPC. Returned: success Sample: "10.0.0.0/16"

return_values.name: ansible_ec2_network_interfaces_macs_mac_address_vpc_ipv6_cidr_blocks
return_values.description: The IPv6 CIDR block of the VPC in which the interface resides. Returned only for instances launched into a VPC. Returned: success Sample: ""

return_values.name: ansible_ec2_placement_availability_zone

return_values.name: ansible_ec2_placement_region
return_values.description: The Region in which the instance launched. Returned: success Sample: "us-east-1"

return_values.name: ansible_ec2_product_codes
return_values.description: Product codes associated with the instance, if any. Returned: success Sample: "aw0evgkw8e5c1q413zgy5pjce"

return_values.name: ansible_ec2_profile
return_values.description: EC2 instance hardware profile. Returned: success Sample: "default-hvm"

return_values.name: ansible_ec2_public_hostname
return_values.description: The instance’s public DNS. If the instance is in a VPC, this category is only returned if the enableDnsHostnames attribute is set to true. Returned: success Sample: "ec2-1-2-3-4.compute-1.amazonaws.com"

return_values.name: ansible_ec2_public_ipv4
return_values.description: The public IPv4 address. If an Elastic IP address is associated with the instance, the value returned is the Elastic IP address. Returned: success Sample: "1.2.3.4"

return_values.name: ansible_ec2_public_key
return_values.description: Public key. Only available if supplied at instance launch time. Returned: success Sample: ""

return_values.name: ansible_ec2_ramdisk_id
return_values.description: The ID of the RAM disk specified at launch time, if applicable. Returned: success Sample: ""

return_values.name: ansible_ec2_reservation_id
return_values.description: The ID of the reservation. Returned: success Sample: "r-0123456789abcdef0"

return_values.name: ansible_ec2_security_groups
return_values.description: The names of the security groups applied to the instance. After launch, you can only change the security groups of instances running in a VPC. Such changes are reflected here and in network/interfaces/macs/mac/security-groups. Returned: success Sample: "securitygroup1,securitygroup2"

return_values.name: ansible_ec2_services_domain
return_values.description: The domain for AWS resources for the region; for example, amazonaws.com for us-east-1. Returned: success Sample: "amazonaws.com"

return_values.name: ansible_ec2_services_partition
return_values.description: The partition that the resource is in. For standard AWS regions, the partition is aws. If you have resources in other partitions, the partition is aws-partitionname. For example, the partition for resources in the China (Beijing) region is aws-cn. Returned: success Sample: "aws"

return_values.name: ansible_ec2_spot_termination_time
return_values.description: The approximate time, in UTC, that the operating system for your Spot instance will receive the shutdown signal. This item is present and contains a time value only if the Spot instance has been marked for termination by Amazon EC2. The termination-time item is not set to a time if you terminated the Spot instance yourself. Returned: success Sample: "2015-01-05T18:02:00Z"

return_values.name: ansible_ec2_user_data
return_values.description: The instance user data. Returned: success Sample: "#!/bin/bash"
